chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Basir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'How did they answer while they were particles?' He said: 'He placed in them that which, when He asked them, they could answer with — meaning regarding the Covenant.'

key_terms.الْمِيثَاقُ: al-mithaq — the primordial Covenant; the pre-eternal agreement described in Quran 7:172 where all souls testified to God's lordship
key_terms.جَعَلَ: ja'ala — He placed/made; refers to God's act of endowing souls with the faculty of response within the state of dharr
key_terms.ذَرٌّ: dharr — primordial particles or atoms; the pre-worldly form in which human souls existed before being placed in bodies

ai.seo_question: How did human souls answer God in the primordial Covenant if they only existed as particles (dharr)?
ai.summary: Abu Basir asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) how human souls were able to respond to God's question in the primordial Covenant (Mithaq), given that they existed only as the smallest particles (dharr). The Imam explains that God had placed within those particles the very capacity to respond — an innate capability that enabled them to affirm divine lordship. This hadith clarifies the mechanism underlying Quran 7:172 (the Covenant of Alast), where God asked 'Am I not your Lord?' and all souls replied 'Yes, we testify.' The concept of dharr (primordial particles) refers to the pre-worldly existence of human souls before their embodiment.
